disagreements.topic: Whether the CEO's 2026 share sales were under a Rule 10b5-1 plan
disagreements.positions: The round-1 supervisor said the CEO's March and June 2026 sales were made under a 10b5-1 plan adopted Mar 3 2026 (it cited a MarketScreener summary). In round 2, agent_3 disagrees, citing the primary Form 4s and Form 144s. The other agents accepted the round-1 correction or did not address it.
disagreements.resolution: agent_3 is right, and the round-1 supervisor's correction was wrong. All of CEO Arash Adam Foroughi's Form 4s for the Mar 11-12 and Jun 10-12 2026 sales have the Rule 10b5-1 box set to false, and none has a plan footnote. His June Form 144s leave the plan-adoption date blank. The Mar 3 2026 plan in the Q1 10-Q belongs to director Maynard Webb (up to 40,000 shares), not to the CEO, and the 10-Q says no other officer or director adopted a plan that quarter. So the CEO's sales (about $51m in June at $473-517, plus March sales) were discretionary open-window sales, made inside the Talbot class period. This strengthens the class action's scienter argument a little. It has no direct effect on earnings, so it does not move the ladder.

disagreements.topic: Size of the FY27 EPS haircut and the multiple, which set the fair-value spread ($310-348)
disagreements.positions: Haircuts now run 3.5-5% (agent_2 3.5%, agent_1 4%, agent_5 4.5%, agents 3 and 4 5%). Multiples run from 15x NTM (agent_5) to 16x NTM (agent_1), or 17-18x FY27 (about 14.5-16x NTM) for agents 3 and 4. FCF required yields are 6-6.5%.
disagreements.resolution: This is now judgment, not fact. All five agree on the facts behind the haircut: Edgewater's Q4 gap is about 1-2%, Wells Fargo's traffic-weighted pixel data says e-commerce is a 2027 story, and revisions are still negative. agent_1's 16x NTM bakes in a re-rating that has not started while revisions are still falling. agent_4's 6.5% FCF yield and 12x EBITDA are at the cheap end. I reconcile at about $322, close to the $326 mean, and leave the ladder at the mean.
disagreements.evidence: Agent files (round 2); Alpha Vantage consensus as cited by all five (FY27 EPS $20.00, was $21.16).

disagreements.topic: How much Unity competition should weigh (Vector growth, the AppLovin v. Unity suit)
disagreements.positions: agent_2 cuts its multiple to 15.5x for the AppLovin v. Unity suit filed Sep 30-Oct 1. agent_4 adds Unity Vector's +23% q/q as spread pressure. The others weigh Unity only through Edgewater.
disagreements.resolution: Confirmed but sized. Unity's Q2 2026 Strategic Grow revenue was $329m (+63% y/y), and it guides Q3 to $380-385m (+68-70% y/y, about +16% q/q). That is faster than AppLovin's Q3 guide of about +7.6% q/q on $1.92B. In dollars, though, AppLovin still adds about $146m a quarter against Unity's about $53m. The suit is real: a TRO application in SF Superior Court plus a JAMS arbitration over Unity's Ad Quality SDK collecting MAX auction data. Unity calls it a response to 'increased competition and slowing growth'. This supports the bear-case weights the agents already use (22-30%). It is not new information that justifies moving the ladder further.
disagreements.evidence: Unity 8-K Ex.99.1, Q2 2026 (Aug 6 2026); MobileGamer.biz, citing Digiday and the court filings (Oct 1 2026).

disagreements.topic: Date of the Q3 2026 report (Nov 4 vs Nov 11)
disagreements.positions: agents 1 and 4 say about Nov 4 (MarketBeat); agents 2 and 3 say Nov 11 (TipRanks); agent_5 says Nov 4-11.
disagreements.resolution: The company has not announced a date as of Oct 2. Its IR feed shows no 'to Announce Third Quarter' release. The pattern points to Wednesday Nov 4: Q1 was announced Apr 1 for May 6 (a Wednesday), and Q2 was announced Jul 1 for Aug 5 (a Wednesday). Both dates fall outside the 1-month window, so the 1-month ladder does not change. The date matters for the timing of the first tranche.
disagreements.evidence: AppLovin IR press-release feed (investors.applovin.com), checked Oct 2 2026; EDGAR shows no 8-K since Aug 5.

disagreements.positions: agent_1 now uses $551m in Q2 (down from about $1B in Q1) and about 326M shares by Oct 2027. The others use 326-330M.
disagreements.resolution: Confirmed. The Q2 10-Q shows 3.28M shares repurchased for $1.5B in H1 2026, with $1.8B of authorization left. That fits about $0.95B in Q1 and $0.55B in Q2. A share count of 326-330M by Oct 2027 is reasonable. It moves fair value by about 1%.

one_month_reasoning: No AppLovin catalyst falls in Oct 2-30. The company has not set a Q3 date, and its pattern points to Wed Nov 4. The Nov 16 lead-plaintiff deadline is also outside. What remains is two-sided: the date announcement, a possible TRO ruling in AppLovin v. Unity, Meta and Alphabet Q3 prints in late October, the Oct 27-28 FOMC, and sell-side alt-data notes, which have moved the stock 3-5% in a day. So I keep the agents' near-symmetric mean around spot (monthly sigma about 21%).
confidence_reason: The five revised ladders sit within about 0.05 of each other at every strike, and all of them already reflect the round-1 findings. My checks overturned one round-1 supervisor fact (the CEO's sales were discretionary, not under a 10b5-1 plan) and confirmed that Unity's competition is real. Both matter for litigation and the bear-case weight, not for the centre of the distribution. None settles a disagreement that clearly moves the forecast, so I keep the mean.
thesis_break_reason: At about $185 the stock trades at about 9x FY27 consensus EPS ($20), about 7-8x EBITDA and a 10%+ FCF yield, with about $0.46B of net debt and $1.8B of buyback authorization left. A sustained trade there would mean the market expects earnings to fall, not just growth to slow. Likely causes: a Q4 guide implying flat or negative q/q revenue, visible MAX/Axon share or spread loss to Unity Vector (now growing about 16% q/q), a loss in the Unity dispute that exposes MAX auction data, an Apple/Google platform action, or a damaging litigation development. The agents' mean is $185 (range $180-195); it sits about one 12-month sigma below spot.
key_drivers: Q3 2026 print (likely Wed Nov 4, unconfirmed) against the $2.055-2.085B guide, and above all the Q4 guide against Edgewater's +8-9% q/q (about $2.25B) and the about $2.27-2.28B consensus.

Gaming share and spreads against Unity: Unity Strategic Grow guided +68-70% y/y for Q3 (about +16% q/q) against AppLovin's about +7.6% q/q; the AppLovin v. Unity TRO/arbitration over MAX auction data.
Whether e-commerce/self-serve adoption shows up on traffic-weighted data (Wells Fargo: about 85% of new pixel sites have no traffic; a '2027 story').
Estimate revisions: FY27 EPS went from $21.16 to $20.00 in 60 days (19 down / 5 up). The 14x multiple will not re-rate until revisions turn.

Valuation floor and capital return: about 14x FY27 EPS and about 6% FCF yield, $1.5B bought back in H1 2026 with $1.8B left, net debt about $0.46B. Legal overhang: two class actions, made somewhat stronger by the CEO's discretionary sales of about $51m in June 2026 inside the class period.

fair_value.reason: FY27 EPS of about $19.2 (consensus $20.00 less about 4%), rolled to an NTM EPS of about $22 at Oct 2027, at about 15x = about $330. Cross-checks: FY27E FCF of about $6.4B / about 328M shares at a 6-6.3% yield = about $310-325; EV/EBITDA of 11-12x on about $8.1B less $0.46B net debt = about $290-320. Blended about $322, against the agents' $310-348 (mean $326). I give a little less weight to agent_1's 16x NTM re-rating, which revisions do not yet support. Share base: 335.3M at Jun 30 2026, falling to about 326-330M with buybacks.

summary: The five revised forecasts agree closely: median about $300, P(>= $281 on 2027-10-01) about 0.55, fair values $310-348. The stock is about 14x FY27 EPS and about a 6% FCF yield after a 60% de-rating. My checks reversed one round-1 supervisor fact: the CEO's 2026 sales were discretionary, not under a 10b5-1 plan, which adds a little to the class-action risk. They also confirmed that Unity is growing about twice as fast as AppLovin sequentially and that the two are now in litigation over MAX data. Neither moves the centre, so I keep the mean ladder (low confidence) with fair value about $322 and thesis break $185. The Q3 print and Q4 guide, likely Nov 4, are the next real test.

sizing.conviction_label_reason: The checked evidence gives a modest expected-return edge (fair value about $322, about +14%), but at about 70-75% realized volatility no fact I verified shows a clear edge over SPY per unit of risk: the stock needs a gain of roughly 30%+ (to about $365) to win on Sharpe, and the ladder gives that only about 0.36.
sizing.entry: 2 tranches: half after the Q3 2026 print and Q4 guide (likely Nov 4), half after the Q4 report in Feb 2027 if the guide holds and revisions stop falling
sizing.overlap: GOOGL (digital ad demand and AI ad tooling; Google AdMob is a direct mediation/network competitor), and to a lesser degree BKNG (performance-marketing spend) and AVGO/NFLX (high-beta growth/AI sentiment)
sizing.reason: Realized vol is about 75%, with several 5-20% one-day gaps this year, and the Q3 print lands in about 5 weeks. Revisions are still negative, two securities class actions are pending (the CEO's discretionary sales inside the class period make them somewhat stronger), and Unity competition is escalating. The valuation support is real but conviction is low, so cap at about 2.5% of the about $10k portfolio, slightly below the round-1 3%.
